notes:
What's new in Vekrun 0.7.1: start in Claude Code or Codex, continue in Vekrun, verify, and hand it back — plus Figma

• Send this to Vekrun: in Claude Code or Codex, say "Send this to Vekrun." The agent captures its work in progress — changed files, decisions, what's done and what remains — and Vekrun opens on an incoming handoff. Your own checkout is never touched (checked before and after), and only the files the agent declared come over; anything else waits for your decision.
• Choose what happens next: Continue implementation, Verify existing implementation (Vekrun checks the work independently and changes nothing), or Review and improve — and which agent continues: Claude, Codex or a Council. Proposed acceptance criteria stay proposals until you tick them.
• Hand it back: when the Work Item finishes, Vekrun offers to return it to the agent it came from — "Fork original session" where the CLI can continue from a copy of the original conversation, or "Start with transferred context". Nothing leaves Vekrun until you allow it; the return says exactly what was verified.
• Connect your coding agents from Connections → External agents: Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, Cursor and VS Code, each with its own token bound to the projects you choose. You see the exact config change first; your other settings are kept and backed up. (Gemini CLI is not yet verified end to end: Google no longer accepts personal sign-ins for it.)
• Figma: connect from Integrations with a personal access token (or a Figma app), try a frame link, and use a Figma frame in the composer with @figma or by pasting a link. Vekrun keeps an unchanging snapshot of the design, plans against it, and can check the built page against the frame: differences are shown by region, and anything it can't compare is reported as unknown, never as a pass. Design changes are detected, and approved criteria are never changed silently. Figma Make code can come in as an export or through an agent that has Figma's own MCP; a comment can be posted back to the frame with your approval. Figma's remote MCP needs Figma to approve Vekrun first.
• Stronger verification everywhere: a criterion that says "always" is checked over a stated range of inputs and reported as "verified within" that range — examples alone never count; each criterion shows how it was checked and how strong the evidence is. A run that needed no change is still verified in a fresh VM. A rejected check gets one more try with the reviewer's reason.
• Security: two adversarial rounds found and fixed 24 real issues across the new connection points — tokens, cross-project access, malicious patches and file names, hidden secrets, design text, and client configs — and all of them stay in the test suite.
• Readiness checks never pile up, and the app can hold far more open files (fixes "unable to open database file" and missing commits on large repositories on slow machines).
